'''Bob Hale''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]] (1945 – 12 December 2017)<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/philosophy/news/memorial-notice-1.752700|title=Memorial Notice for Bob Hale|date=18 December 2017|publisher=Sheffield Department of Philosophy}}</ref> was a British philosopher, known for his contributions to the development of the [[Neo-logicism|neo-Fregean]] (neo-logicist) [[philosophy of mathematics]] in collaboration with [[Crispin Wright]], and for his works in [[Modal logic|modality]] and [[philosophy of language]].<ref name=3am>{{citation|title=Bob Hale RIP (1945–2017)|url=http://www.3ammagazine.com/3am/bob-hale-rip-1945-2017/|magazine=[[3:AM Magazine]]|date=16 December 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==
Hale obtained a BPhil in Philosophy in 1967 from [[Linacre College]], [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{citation|url=
https://www.linacre.ox.ac.uk/sites/default/files/magazine-pdfs/issue_54.pdf|title=Linacre News, Issue 54|date=Autumn 2017|publisher=Linacre College}}</ref> From 2006 until his death, he was a professor of [[philosophy]] in the department of philosophy at the [[University of Sheffield]]. Prior to that, he taught in the [[University of Glasgow]], the [[University of St. Andrews]] and the [[University of Lancaster]].

Hale produced the first published neo-Fregean [[construction of the real numbers]].<ref name=3am/><ref name=profile>{{cite web|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/philosophy/staff/profiles/hale |title=Profile: Bob Hale | publisher = Sheffield Department of Philosophy | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160921114320/https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/philosophy/staff/profiles/hale | archive-date = 21 September 2016}}</ref> In his book (''Necessary Beings''), he argues for an essentialist theory of necessity and possibility.<ref name=profile/>

== Notable positions ==
* [[British Academy]] Research Reader (1997–99)
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (from 2000)<ref name=profile/>
* President of the [[Aristotelian Society]] (2002–03)<ref>[http://www.aristoteliansociety.org.uk/about/the-council/ The Council], The Aristotelian Society, retrieved 2012-12-03.</ref>
* [[Leverhulme]] Senior Research Fellow (2009–11)
